name: Facet
text:
Implement a dark theme by default with a highly visible light-theme toggle. This keeps the benefits of dark themes for data visualization—better contrast, reduced eye strain, and alignment with industry standards—while giving users control to switch when needed. The trade-off is a slight increase in interface complexity, but the toggle’s prominence minimizes the risk of users ignoring warnings. A quick user test will confirm the toggle’s discoverability and task performance.

name: Pane
text: A toggle adds friction—users won’t switch unless forced, and forcing breaks the "quality first" rule. Instead, auto-switch based on ambient light or task type: dark for data-heavy screens, light for text-heavy workflows. Settle it with a 5-user hallway test: measure completion time and error rates for both modes.
